locator.text: Equation (5.8), p. 48, in the proof of Lemma 5.1

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. Same shape, strictly larger right-hand side. Term by term: p_k matches exactly (halfLength k = (k+1)/2 = ⌈k/2⌉); the Cauchy budget is split among the derivative letters only, as in the paper (word_radialBound, line 331); the radial/simplex factor is r^k/k! with r ≤ T = a, and the coefficient factor is M^k with M the row-sum bound on A₀ and A₁. Three differences. (i) The factorial is k!, not (k+1)!: the Lean counts only the k letters of the word and carries the final G inside the constant B bounding the input field F = G f_n (RadialBound … B 0), where the paper counts k+1 integrations and gets a^{k+1}/(k+1)!. (ii) The factor 2^k counting the compositions is left explicit instead of being absorbed into C_n^{k+1} as the paper does. (iii) The Cauchy factor is (max{1,Δ⁻¹} · max{1,p_k})^{p_k} rather than (max{1,p_k/Δ})^{p_k}; the two agree when Δ ≤ 1, and the Lean's is larger when Δ > 1. Each of (i)–(iii) is absorbable into a constant of the paper's own form C_n^{k+1} (since (k+1)·2^k ≤ 4^k), and none affects what the paper uses (5.8) for: summability is proved in summable_wordLayers (524) and used for convergence of the series. Also, the norm: the paper's S_{ρ'} = {η : dist(η,[−1,1]) < ρ'} is a neighborhood of the segment, whereas the Lean estimate is a sup over a closed parameter disk closedBall c ρ (with closedBall c σ inside the domain) and over the whole radial interval; applying it at each center c ∈ [−1,1] with σ = ρ_paper, ρ = ρ' covers S_{ρ'} with the same gap Δ.
